content.body:
The Lockheed P-38F, which also saw service in the French Air Force, were excellent twin-engine fighters, which were considered a very avant garde design at the time.
The centerline guns package is very deadly, with almost unparalleled firepower due to the extremely tight grouping of the heavy caliber guns. The P-38 is a very large wingspan fighter design, having twin engines and twin tail booms. It doesn’t roll very fast and the ailerons are heavy, however with some of the advanced Fowler type wing flaps deployed, your turn rate can increase to a very significant degree. Be warned the P-38 can turn very tightly and very fast when called upon to do so. You do need to be careful of the extra drag created by it's size and weight when you are flaps down ... because if you fail to get a guns solution early you will bleed off valuable speed if you continue to turn with flaps down for extended periods of time.
P-38s do not accelerate quickly or climb particularly fast, but they do enjoy good level speed at low altitudes and have excellent diving acceleration like most American designs.
Fly the P-38 in pairs with a wingman, stay fast and use speed and let the hard-hitting guns package to do the job. Avoid sustained turning fights unless you have the enemy outnumbered or you are certain of a victorious guns solution in the early part of the turning duel.
